function.name: uber_eat_order
function.description: Place an order for food delivery on Uber Eats by specifying the restaurant and the items with their respective quantities. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

restaurant.description: The name of the restaurant from which to order food.

items.description: A list of food item names selected for the order.

quantities.description: A list of quantities for each food item, corresponding by index to the items array.

message.content: I’m sorry, but I don’t have access to real‑time weather data. You can check a reliable weather website or app (e.g., Weather.com, AccuWeather, or your local meteorological service) for the current temperature in Moscow.
message.reasoning: The user asks: "What weather is now in Moscow, in Celsius?" They want current weather in Moscow. We need to provide the current temperature in Celsius. We don't have real-time data. We can either say we can't fetch real-time data or we can simulate. According to policy, we should not fabricate. We can say we cannot provide real-time data. But maybe we can use a weather API? There's no tool for that. So we should respond that we cannot fetch real-time data. Alternatively, we could ask them to check a weather website. So answer: I don't have real-time data.
